title: LIFO-Backpressure Achieves Near Optimal Utility-Delay Tradeoff
citation_details: 3 Apr 2011 (arXiv preprint; journal version in IEEE/ACM Trans. Netw. 21(3):831-844, 2012)
paper_overview: This paper proves that combining the standard Backpressure (MaxWeight / QLA) algorithm with a Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) queueing discipline achieves a time-average utility within O(1/V) of optimal while keeping the average delay of all but an O(1/V^{log V}) fraction of traffic bounded by O([log V]^2) under general finite-state Markovian network dynamics, without requiring statistical knowledge of the network randomness or pre-estimated Lagrange multipliers. All four inventoried claims are established theorems (no conjectures are stated); Theorems 2 and 3 cite proofs in companion papers bundled under references/.

folio.blurb: Under LIFO-Backpressure with control parameter V >= 1, all but an O(1/V^{log V}) fraction of arriving packets depart with average delay at most [2D + 2K(log V)^2 + delta_max] / lambda_tilde_j = O([log V]^2).

figure.alt: Simulated single-queue backlog trajectory under Backpressure fluctuating within an O([log V]^2) band around the Theta(V) dual attractor gamma_V^*, paired with a LIFO queue diagram showing arrivals entering and departing inside [Q_Low, Q_High] atop the Theta(V) base backlog.
figure.caption: Fig. 1. The LIFO-Backpressure Idea: exponential attraction keeps the backlog within an O([log V]^2) band [Q_Low, Q_High] around gamma_V^*, so LIFO serves almost all arriving packets from the top band.
